defectInAnEvidenceArtifactNotInThePacket.whyItMatters: actual-writes.json is the byte-proof report a downstream lane reads to decide whether a known prefill reached the page. A verifier that trusted it would fail a correct family on four missing prefills. A verifier that read only the headline valuesReportedByFinalizer 6 would pass it without noticing the per-field evidence contradicts the headline. Both readings are available in the same file, which is the thing to fix.
defectInAnEvidenceArtifactNotInThePacket.whatItIsNot: not a packet defect. The packet is correct. Nothing in the overlay needs re-rendering for this.
defectInAnEvidenceArtifactNotInThePacket.contrastWithVermont: this is the mirror image of the defect this worker found in vt_seal_18_to_21-set and vt_seal_dui-set, where the report claimed a write the bytes did not carry. Here the bytes carry a write the report does not claim. Both are the same underlying thing: a read-back that cannot be trusted in either direction.

observationForProductAndCounsel.what: On the boundary fixture two participant facts do not fit their widgets at the six-point minimum font: a 50-character docket number needing 173pt and a 70-character legal name needing 195.6pt, in a 159.84pt box.
observationForProductAndCounsel.howTheBuilderHandledIt: declared, measured and refused — value, reason, widget width, required width and minimum font size all recorded. Not clipped, not shrunk past legibility, not silently dropped. That is the right behaviour.
observationForProductAndCounsel.theQuestionItRaises: a real participant whose legal name does not fit the widget still has to file. What the packet does for them — an attachment, a continuation, an abbreviation the court accepts — is a product and counsel question, not a build defect, and this lane raises it rather than answering it.
observationForProductAndCounsel.whyItIsRaisedHere: the boundary fixture exists to find exactly this, and it found it. Recording it as an observation is the only way the finding survives past this lane.

buildersClaimUnderTest.howThisLaneTreatedIt: as the claim under test. Taking the builder's own actual-writes.json at face value would have produced four false failures on this family; opening the PDFs produced the truth. PF-C's COMPLETED verdict is not evidence for itself and was not used as any.

factoryCheckNoteForCaptain.check: F24 — one claim ledger grants every dispatched family exactly once, to one lane of each kind
factoryCheckNoteForCaptain.status: FAILING at this head, and it was already failing on Captain's own HEAD ledger before this worker committed anything, which this lane confirmed by running the check against Captain's ledger alone.
factoryCheckNoteForCaptain.observed: 25 grants whose lane is not present in ACTIVE_ASSIGNMENTS.json — VF13 4, VF14 2, VF15 5, VF16 5, VF17 9.
factoryCheckNoteForCaptain.cause: The five cross-verification lanes were minted into the claim ledger without matching lane entries in ACTIVE_ASSIGNMENTS.json. F24 reads a grant whose lane is undispatched as a grant that should not exist.
factoryCheckNoteForCaptain.notCausedByThisLane: VF14's two grants are among the 25, but so are the other four lanes' 23, and the check failed identically with this worker's ledger changes reverted. Releasing the two VF14 grants on completion did not cause it and does not clear it.
factoryCheckNoteForCaptain.notFixedHere: ACTIVE_ASSIGNMENTS.json is a shared dispatch manifest, not this lane's owned path. Adding a VF14 entry would be this verifier dispatching its own lane, would leave the other four lanes still failing, and would turn a real refusal green without fixing what it refuses. This is the third time this shift the mechanism has correctly refused something a dispatch left half-done, and the right answer each time was to hand it back.
factoryCheckNoteForCaptain.theFix: add the five cross-verification lanes to ACTIVE_ASSIGNMENTS.json so every minted grant has a dispatched lane behind it, exactly as the DISC and SRC lanes do.
